subject: Renewal request: pricing rebase + staged capacity ramp / escrow ask
messages:
From: Sasha Miller <sasha@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Owen Blake <owen.blake@acme.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Usage surge + renewal discussion

Hi Irene,

Quick note as we head into our renewal — our Q2 usage ran 2.8x above forecast after we pushed the new personalization pipeline. That puts us in a tough spot for the committed tiers we signed up for last year. We really like the platform and want to expand (adding two more teams), but we need price certainty for the next 12 months while we normalize consumption.

Specifically, two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood offer a rate rebase on baseline token pricing for the renewal window (12 months)?
- Can we stagger the uplift (we plan a 30% capacity ramp over 3 quarters) with an escrow or hold mechanism that protects us from retroactive true-ups while you guarantee reserved capacity?

Owen and I are available for a quick call tomorrow afternoon. Appreciate any initial thoughts.

Thanks,
Sasha
Head of AI Platform
Acme Robotics

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Miller <sasha@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Usage surge + renewal discussion

Hi Sasha — thanks for the context and congrats on the personalization rollout (that spike makes sense). I pulled the Q2 usage report and attached it for transparency.

High level proposal from our side (we can iterate on terms):
1) Staged Rebase: a 10% rate rebase on baseline unit price effective at renewal, with two additional conditional reductions (5% each) tied to usage stabilization milestones across Q1 and Q2 after renewal.
2) Escrow/hold: We can lock the initial rebase for 12 months in exchange for a modest committed uplift (we propose a 15% committed increase over current baseline). Any overage beyond the committed uplift would still be billed at standard overage rates, but we'd provide a 90-day dispute window tied to telemetry.
3) Capacity guarantee: Redwood will reserve dedicated slots to cover the planned 30% ramp; if we miss the ramp, we'll convert unused reserved capacity into credits applied to invoices.

I've looped in Karthik for approval on commercial concessions and Grace from finance to scope the escrow mechanics. Can we take 30 minutes today at 4pm ET to walk through the term sheet? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a draft term sheet (attached).

Best,
Irene
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-usage-q2-2026.csv; redwood-staged-rebase-term-sheet-v1.pdf

From: Owen Blake <owen.blake@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Miller <sasha@acme.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Usage surge + renewal discussion

Thanks, Irene. The staged rebase + escrow approach sounds reasonable — two quick clarifications from our legal/ops team:
- What exactly triggers the conditional reductions? Is it 30-day rolling avg usage within X% of baseline?
- For the escrow, we need the ability to tap credits for legitimate billing disputes or major performance regressions.

If you can put proposed trigger language in the term sheet, we can circulate to procurement today. We can do the 4pm ET sync as well.

—Owen

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Miller <sasha@acme.ai>, Owen Blake <owen.blake@acme.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 11:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Usage surge + renewal discussion

Hi Sasha / Owen — follow-up from today's discussion and next steps:

Summary of agreed points:
- Staged rebase: 10% at renewal, then two conditional 5% drops conditional on 90-day rolling-stability (usage within ±12% of the new baseline) at the end of Q1 and Q2 post-renewal.
- Committed uplift: Acme will commit to a 15% baseline uplift compared to current committed units.
- Escrow mechanics: Redwood will place the delta equal to one month of forecasted spend into an escrow account. That escrow can be applied to billing disputes (validated via telemetry) or converted to credits if reserved capacity was not used due to Redwood-side capacity shortfall. Legal to exchange language via DocuSign.
- Capacity guarantee: Redwood will reserve capacity to support the 30% ramp; any unused reserved capacity at quarter end converts to invoice credit.

Action items:
- Monica: send final term sheet with trigger language to Sasha and Owen by EOD Monday (DocuSign link included).
- Grace: prepare a short escrow SOW for procurement to review.
- Karthik/Irene: prepare the updated pricing schedule for accounts receivable.

Thanks — we aim to have a countersigned amendment in place before the current term expires on 2026-09-15.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Account Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-staged-rebase-term-sheet-v1.pdf
